events_utc.event: Unretrieved ConnectionResetError during POST /invoices/101/refund; HTTP 404 completed
Unretrieved ConnectionResetError during POST /invoices/101/note; HTTP 404 completed
Allocation cleanup phase=http fails with ConnectionResetError

live.impact: Local Runtime process disappears, allocation execution report unavailable and public metrics partial. Emergency telemetry flush did preserve all 404 spans.
live.recovery: Existing manage.py runtime 3 restored the same configured Runtime; all four local and two cloud agents were idle afterwards.

root_cause: An early HTTP response closes the target connection while the POST body remains unread. This can produce an ordinary TCP reset after the response is complete.

CPython StreamReaderProtocol.connection_lost stores ConnectionResetError in its completed close waiter and closes the socket. Every later StreamWriter.wait_closed awaits that same completed Future and raises the same exception object.
OwnedHandler.close_writer calls task.result before discarding the writer. That exception therefore retains a physically closed writer in self.writers.
The native connection task can already have been removed from transports before wrapper cleanup raises, producing Task exception was never retrieved.
OwnedHandler.join retries close_writer for retained writers outside its gather-result OSError filter. The cached reset poisons every subsequent cleanup attempt.
MitmproxyEngine never reaches final process-state restoration; allocation lifecycle treats cleanup as unconfirmed and deliberately fences and exits with code 70.

control_tests.notes: Existing graceful closure and genuine writer/file failure tests pass; missing real TCP-reset close coverage explains the gap.

proposed_correction: Distinguish a completed socket close carrying a network termination error from a genuinely unconfirmed cleanup failure; retire the writer after the former.
Keep native task outcomes owned/observed and ensure expected peer resets do not escape as unhandled task errors.
Preserve fail-closed behavior for genuinely unjoined I/O, timeout, callback bugs or file-removal failures; do not globally swallow Exception or disable exit 70.

Cover programmatic HTTP and scanner ingress using the shared OwnedHandler, plain/TLS paths, completed-response and mid-response resets, cancellation, no replay, full erasure and next-allocation reuse.
